people.name: Gianni Infantino
people.notes: 9th FIFA President since 26 February 2016; re-elected 2019 and 2023. Confirmed current as of 2026 via inside.fifa.com pages and Wikipedia (incumbent). Cross-checked: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianni_Infantino

people.name: Mattias Grafström
people.notes: Appointed Secretary General by FIFA Council on 15 May 2024 (acting from 31 Dec 2023). Confirmed incumbent as of 2026 via Wikipedia (last edited Apr 2026) and recent 2026 inside.fifa.com news. Cross-checked: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattias_Grafstr%C3%B6m

people.name: Arsène Wenger
people.notes: Appointed Chief of Global Football Development on 13 November 2019. Still in role per 2026 World Cup Technical Study Group coverage and Wikipedia. Cross-checked: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ars%C3%A8ne_Wenger

people.name: Thomas Peyer
people.notes: Appointed Chief Finance Officer effective 5 September 2016 (FIFA uses 'Chief Finance Officer', not 'Chief Financial Officer'). Confirmed still in role at 73rd FIFA Congress (2023) page: https://inside.fifa.com/watch/73rd-fifa-congress-fifa-chief-finance-officer-thomas-peyer . Could not find a dated June-2026 page explicitly reconfirming he still holds the title; no contradicting departure found. No Wikipedia article.

people.name: Kevin Lamour
people.notes: Joined FIFA as Chief Operating Officer effective 1 November 2024 (from UEFA). Oversees Audit & Advisory, Communications, Finance, Legal & Compliance, Member Associations, People, Technology & Operations, Professional Football Relations and Development, and Social Responsibility & Education. No 2026-dated departure found; assumed current. No Wikipedia article.

people.name: Manolo Zubiria
people.role: FIFA World Cup 2026 Chief Tournament Officer – USA
people.notes: Exact title 'FIFA World Cup 2026 Chief Tournament Officer – USA' quoted verbatim on official inside.fifa.com 2026 media release. In role since August 2023; also FIFA Director of Competitions. No Wikipedia article (Wikidata-only / disambiguation with a 19th-century namesake).

people.name: Heimo Schirgi
people.role: FIFA Chief Event Operations Officer (also Chief Operating Officer, FIFA26 tournament delivery organisation)
people.notes: Official inside.fifa.com (2026 Atlanta workshop article) gives title 'FIFA's Chief Event Operations Officer'. Multiple 2026 outlets also style him 'FIFA World Cup 2026 Chief Operating Officer' for the FIFA26 North American delivery org. Senior officer responsible for World Cup 26 operations. No Wikipedia article.

people.name: Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa
people.role: FIFA Senior Vice-President; FIFA Council Vice-President (AFC President)
people.notes: FIFA Senior Vice-President (since 2018) and AFC President (since 2013). Named as Senior Vice-President in a FIFA Council meeting photo caption on the inside.fifa.com secretary-general page. Wikipedia last updated Apr 2026 lists him as Senior Vice-President of FIFA Council.

people.name: Aleksander Čeferin
people.notes: UEFA President since 2016, automatically a FIFA Vice-President; re-elected UEFA 2023. Listed on FIFA Council Wikipedia page as a Vice-President. Cross-checked: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksander_%C4%8Ceferin

people.name: Sándor Csányi
people.notes: FIFA Vice-President (UEFA quota) since Feb 2019; re-elected at 47th UEFA Congress (April 2023, term to 2027). Source corrected on re-check: confirmed via his Wikipedia article and the Hungarian FA announcement.

people.name: Debbie Hewitt
people.notes: FIFA Vice-President elected 5 April 2023 (first female FIFA VP; four-year term). FA Chair, reappointed Dec 2024 (term Jan 2025-Jan 2028). Source corrected on re-check: The FA's official announcement.

people.name: Victor Montagliani
people.notes: CONCACAF President and FIFA Vice-President since 12 May 2016. Wikipedia (last edited 4 May 2026) lists both roles as incumbent.

people.name: Alejandro Domínguez
people.notes: CONMEBOL President since 2016 (re-elected, term to 2029), a FIFA Vice-President and FIFA Council member. Named in a FIFA Council meeting photo caption on inside.fifa.com. Wikipedia title disambiguated as '(football executive)'.

people.name: Patrice Motsepe
people.notes: CAF President since 2021, re-elected 12 March 2025; serves as a FIFA Vice-President. Named in a FIFA Council meeting photo caption on the inside.fifa.com secretary-general page.

people.name: Lambert Maltock
people.notes: OFC President and FIFA Council member since 2019 (re-elected OFC 2023); serves as a FIFA Vice-President. Named in a FIFA Council meeting photo caption on the inside.fifa.com secretary-general page.
